subject.title: Dashboard: widget write-back — a setState bridge capability + persisted widget state

question: Should OpenClaw accept a bundled dashboard widget write-back capability now, and should its persistent state use plugin-owned SQLite or another approved store instead of per-widget JSON files?
rationale: The request is useful and fits the dashboard roadmap, but it changes iframe-to-parent trust, plugin API/storage contracts, and persisted state behavior that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Sponsor with storage and security design
options.body: Proceed after the dashboard base lands, requiring a reviewed bridge contract, approval semantics, SQLite or approved storage design, and adversarial regression tests.

options.title: Defer under the roadmap
options.body: Keep this open under the Wave 2 tracker until the dashboard base PRs settle and maintainers can evaluate the added security surface.

options.title: Reject bundled write-back for now
options.body: Close the direction if maintainers decide stateful custom widgets should remain outside bundled OpenClaw until a separate plugin or ClawHub surface proves demand.

recommendation.title: Sponsor with storage and security design
recommendation.body: Proceed after the dashboard base lands, requiring a reviewed bridge contract, approval semantics, SQLite or approved storage design, and adversarial regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-main owner signal for the Control UI plugin-tab seam that this capability would extend.
